5 finalists, 3 routines each and 1 mirrorball trophy up for grabs
Your last chance to hear "Thanks, Alfonso" is right around the corner. Well, until next season.

The Dancing With The Stars Season 35 finale airs Tuesday, Nov. 24. Five stars remain: Olympic figure Skater Amber Glenn, comedian and podcaster Connor Wood, Paralympic gold medallist Ezra Frech, reality star Maura Higgins and actor Tatyana Ali.
The three-hour finale will air live on Disney+ in Canada, with each couple performing three (yes, that's right, three) routines.

There's the judges' choice, where a judge assigns a specific dance style and song to each finalist. Then there's the instant dance, where couples find out what they're doing on the fly. And of course, there's the freestyle, where pretty much anything goes — it's a fan favourite for a reason.

items: How Dancing with the Stars became must-watch TV in the streaming era

blocks.text: Now, in typical reality television fashion, we're not nearing the end without a hint of internet drama.

Following a semifinal elimination that sent Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson home despite a streak of perfect scores, some viewers threatened boycotts, arguing the show has become a popularity contest since Connor Wood is at the bottom of the leaderboard.
Speaking to E! News, Shum said he thinks "social media is a little nuts" and that he hopes the show addresses it at some point.

"I think there's a good amount of bullying that doesn't feel really good, and I think the rest of the cast feels it," he said, sharing that he loved the experience and that every cast member "has been able to do something incredible in our own way."
Season 27 winner Bobby Bones defended Wood on TikTok, calling a "toxic" fraction of Dancing With the Stars fans "the biggest losers in the whole world" after seeing Shum speak out.
Whether you’re watching to see who wins or just here for the choreography, here’s what you can expect for the last night in the ballroom:
Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov
Judges' choice: Quickstep to Sing, Sing, Sing by Louis Prima.
Freestyle: Like a Prayer and Music by Madonna.
Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold
Judges' choice: Viennese Waltz to Willing and Able by Noah Kahan.
Freestyle: Singin' in the Rain by Gene Kelly and Umbrella by Rihanna.
Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach
Judges' choice: Salsa to Danza Kuduro by Don Omar feat. Lucenzo.
Freestyle: Numb by Linkin Park.
Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas
Judges' choice: Tango to Gallo Ciego by Orquesta Color Tango.
Freestyle: Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend by Marilyn Monroe and Irish folk songs The Parting Glass and Flowers of the Red Hill.
Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik
Judges' choice: Salsa to Jamaican (Bam Bam) by Hugel & Solto (FR).
Freestyle: Minnie the Moocher by Cab Calloway and Over the Rainbow by Judy Garland.
